Three outcomes have resulted: entropy has increased, some energy has become unavailable to do work, and the system has become less orderly. Let us think about each of these results.First, entropy has increased for the same reason that it did in the example above. Mixing the two bodies of water has the same effect as heat transfer from the hot one and the same heat transfer into the cold one. Entropy is also associated with the tendency toward disorder in an isolated system.

A gas initially occupies one half of an insulated container; the other half is a vacuum. A partition is removed, and the gas expands freely into the empty half. (a) Why is this process irreversible? (b) No heat is transferred during the expansion. Does this mean that the gas’s entropy remains unchanged? Explain why substituting Q=0 into ΔS=QrevT, the relation for reversible heat transfer at constant temperature, would not correctly determine the entropy change in this free expansion.
